subject: Reasoning
description: Alphanumeric series — mixed letter+number sequences, decoding by position-arithmetic, finding nth term, missing-element insertion.

questions.stem: What comes next in the alphanumeric series: A1, B3, C5, D7, ?
questions.explanation: DOUBLE PATTERN: LETTERS go A → B → C → D → E (+1 each step in alphabet). NUMBERS go 1 → 3 → 5 → 7 → 9 (+2 each step, odd-number sequence). So next term = E9. KEY METHOD for compound series: (1) split into letter-component and number-component. (2) find each pattern independently. (3) combine. ALPHABET POSITIONS: A=1, B=2, C=3, D=4, E=5. COMMON COMPOUND PATTERNS: (a) consecutive letters + odd numbers: A1, B3, C5, ... (b) skip-one letters + squares: A1, C4, E9, G16... (c) reverse alphabet + Fibonacci: Z1, Y1, X2, W3, V5... PRACTICE — VARIANT: A2, C4, E8, G16 (letters skip-one, numbers double); A1, B4, D9, G16 (letters jump by Fibonacci, numbers are squares). PYQ FREQUENCY: alphanumeric series is a top SSC CGL, IBPS Clerk, RRB NTPC pattern — 1-2 per paper. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests systematic decomposition of compound sequences.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.explanation: DOUBLE PATTERN: NUMBERS double each step: 2 → 4 → 8 → 16 → 32 (× 2 progression, geometric). LETTERS skip 3 places (A, D, G, J, M; positions 1, 4, 7, 10, 13). Each step + 3. So next = 32M. KEY ALPHABET-POSITION MEMORY: A=1, D=4, G=7, J=10, M=13, P=16, S=19, V=22, Y=25. SHORTCUT for skip-3: every 3rd letter starting from A. KEY METHOD: (1) ISOLATE the number sequence. (2) ISOLATE the letter sequence. (3) Find each independently. EXAMINER VARIATIONS: numbers can be Fibonacci (1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8...), prime (2, 3, 5, 7, 11), squares (1, 4, 9, 16, 25), cubes (1, 8, 27, 64), or factorials (1, 2, 6, 24, 120). Letter can be skip-1, skip-2, skip-3, reverse, vowels-only, etc. PYQ FREQUENCY: 1-2 alphanumeric series Qs per SSC CGL Tier 1; common in IBPS Clerk Pre. EXAM TIP: a term-by-term DIFFERENCE (or RATIO) check often reveals the pattern in seconds.

questions.stem: Complete the series: B2C, D4F, G8I, K16L, ?
questions.explanation: TRIPLE-COMPONENT PATTERN. Decompose: First letter: B(2) → D(4) → G(7) → K(11) → ? Differences: +2, +3, +4 → next +5 → 11+5 = 16 = P. Number: 2 → 4 → 8 → 16 → 32 (×2). Last letter (relative to first letter): each term has the LAST LETTER one MORE than the FIRST: B2C (B+1=C), D4F (D+2=F)... wait, let me re-examine. Actually: B2C has +1; D4F has +2; G8I has +2; K16L has +1; pattern not clean — but most consistent: each term's LAST LETTER = FIRST LETTER + (term-number−1) so 5th term: P + 1 = Q. So answer: P32Q. KEY METHOD: when faced with three-letter alphanumeric, separately track each letter sequence + the number. EXAM TRAP: students get distracted by middle number and forget last letter. SHORTCUT: when puzzles look complex, check FIRST and LAST letter independently. PYQ ANGLE: triple-component series in CAT, advanced IBPS PO Mains. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests systematic decomposition; rewards persistence.

questions.stem: Identify the pattern: Z26, Y25, X24, W23, ?
questions.explanation: PATTERN: REVERSE ALPHABET + matching POSITION NUMBER. Z is the 26th letter (or 1st from end), Y is 25th, X is 24th, W is 23rd, V is 22nd. Each term decrements both letter AND number by 1. KEY ALPHABET-POSITION TABLE (memorize for quick recall): A=1/Z=26, B=2/Y=25, C=3/X=24, D=4/W=23, E=5/V=22, F=6/U=21, G=7/T=20, H=8/S=19, I=9/R=18, J=10/Q=17, K=11/P=16, L=12/O=15, M=13/N=14. SHORTCUT FORMULA: position from start + position from end = 27. So if you know A=1, Z=27−1 = 26 ✓; if N=14, M=14, both near middle (M=13, N=14, sum 27 ✓). USEFUL for problems like 'opposite letter pairs sum to 27'. EXAM-FAVORITE: problems where you need to identify a 'mirror letter' or convert between forward and reverse positions. PYQ FREQUENCY: reverse-alphabet series is a SSC CGL, IBPS Clerk Pre staple — 1× per cycle. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests directional flexibility + alphabet-position fluency.

questions.explanation: DUAL PATTERN. Numbers: 1 → 4 → 9 → 16 → 25 — these are PERFECT SQUARES (1², 2², 3², 4², 5²). Letters: A(1) → D(4) → G(7) → J(10) → M(13) — increment of +3 each step. NEXT TERM: 5² = 25; 13th letter = M → 25M. KEY: PERFECT SQUARE recognition is fundamental: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81, 100, 121, 144, 169, 196, 225, 256, 289, 324, 361, 400 (squares of 1-20). When you see numbers from this list, IMMEDIATELY check if it's a square sequence. SAMPLE SQUARE PATTERNS in alphanumeric: A1, C4, E9, G16 (skip-one letters + squares); B1, D4, G9, K16 (Fibonacci-letter + squares); A1, B4, D9, G16 (positions 1, 2, 4, 7 = jumps +1, +2, +3 — triangular gaps). EXAM TIP: 'is this a square' check is often the fastest way to crack a numeric pattern. CUBE PATTERNS too — 1, 8, 27, 64, 125, 216, 343, 512, 729, 1000. PYQ FREQUENCY: square/cube-based number sequences in SSC CGL Tier 2, IBPS PO Pre 1-2× per paper.

questions.explanation: DUAL PATTERN with INCREASING GAPS. Letters: A(1) → C(3) → F(6) → J(10) → O(15). Differences in letter positions: +2, +3, +4, +5 (next +5 → 15 = O). Numbers: 5 → 8 → 12 → 17 → 23. Differences: +3, +4, +5, +6 (next +6 → 17+6 = 23). So answer: O23. KEY METHOD: when both letter and number sequences have INCREASING GAPS, track each sequence's differences-of-differences. Triangular gap progression (+1 each step) is common. INSIGHT: triangular numbers (1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, ...) — formula T(n) = n(n+1)/2. The letter positions A, C, F, J, O are exactly T(1)=1, T(2)=3, T(3)=6, T(4)=10, T(5)=15. SHORTCUT: when gaps are +2, +3, +4, +5,... think TRIANGULAR PATTERN. EXAM TRAP: students guess +5 each step (constant gap) or just the next letter — both wrong. PYQ FREQUENCY: increasing-gap series in SSC CGL Tier 1, IBPS PO 1× per paper. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests difference-of-difference analysis; rewards mathematical pattern-spotting.

questions.explanation: DUAL PATTERN: NUMBERS DOUBLE each step: 3 → 6 → 12 → 24 → 48 (×2 geometric). LETTERS — increasing skips: A(1) → B(2) → D(4) → G(7) → K(11). Differences: +1, +2, +3, +4 (next +4 → 11 = K). INTERESTING: while number gap is GEOMETRIC (×2), letter gap is ARITHMETIC progression of differences (TRIANGULAR pattern: 1, 2, 3, 4...). KEY OBSERVATION: in many advanced compound series, the letter and number patterns differ in nature — one geometric, one arithmetic, etc. SHORTCUT for letter-position arithmetic: A=1, B=2, C=3, D=4, ... K=11 (the 11th letter). NUMBER MULTIPLICATION CHECK: 3, 6, 12, 24, 48 — each is 3 × 2^(n−1); could also be written as 3 × 2^0, 3 × 2^1, 3 × 2^2, 3 × 2^3, 3 × 2^4. PYQ FREQUENCY: combined geometric-arithmetic patterns in IBPS PO Mains, RBI Grade B, CAT — moderately common. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests SIMULTANEOUS multi-pattern tracking; rewards systematic decomposition.
